packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 — unverified image reading

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading. Blind reading. I have not tried to identify work or author.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Two faces: image-001 (overview) with tiles image-002 (upper) and image-003 (lower) = "face 1"; image-004 (overview) with tiles image-005 (upper) and image-006 (lower) = "face 2". No scale in the frame.

Observations
- Each face shows a vertical strip of parchment fixed to the inside of a book board as binding material. On face 1 the strip lies at the left (next to the spine/joint), and its right side is covered by a white paper pastedown (which carries the blind impression and ink offset of a printed ornament or initial; not manuscript). On face 2 the strip lies at the right, with bare wooden board and vellum turn-ins to its left; its right edge runs into the joint.
- Text upright on both faces. One column visible on each, cut on both vertical sides: face 1 lacks one to three letters at the left of most lines and everything beyond about 20 characters at the right (hidden under the pastedown or cut); face 2 lacks one to three letters at the left (cut edge against the board) and the line ends at the right (in the joint).
- Top line of each face is cut horizontally through the letters. Below the last line on both faces the parchment is blank, so the text ends at a lower margin: 14 lines visible on each face.
- Script: a large, upright formal book hand (gothic textualis type), dark brown ink, ruled lines visible. Red initials of one-and-a-half to two-line height: face 1 "T" (line 4) and "I" in the left margin (line 10); face 2 "H" (line 6), a letter at the right edge of lines 7-8 (only its left part, "I" or "L"?), and "P" (line 13). A red rubric in the same size of script on face 2 line 3. A paler pinkish "T" between lines 3 and 4 of face 2 looks like an offset or show-through of a red initial, not a letter of this text.
- No running title, gloss, underlining or musical notation.
- Damage: face 1 lines 5-11 abraded and stained brown with small skin losses; face 2 has small losses in lines 6 and 10.

Tentative interpretation
- The short clauses, sentence-opening red initials at regular intervals and the red heading following "Amen." suggest verse in stanzas (each red initial opening a new stanza), written continuously as prose, with a liturgical rubric on face 2. The red initials do not fall at line beginnings, which fits verse written out as prose. I do not infer more.
- Which face comes first is not shown; they may be two sides of one strip or two separate strips.

2. SPANS SELECTED / UNREAD
All 14 lines of each face are transcribed. Unread: the cut top line of each face (only lower halves of letters), and whatever continues under the paper pastedown on face 1. Lifting the pastedown or a transmitted-light image would be needed for the line ends of face 1.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: ( ) = expansion; [lost] = cut away or hidden; {T} = red initial; ? = uncertain. I do not complete words across the cuts.

FACE 1 — image-002 (upper tile; lines from top of image-002)

image-002 L1:  [upper halves cut away; lower halves suggest] …mon..? oz..? adorat?[lost]
image-002 L2:  [lost]onuit ministrum fix[lost]
image-002 L3:  [lost]sequeris me cito pen[lost]
image-002 L4:  [lost]is ad astra. {T}ortor ir[lost]
image-002 L5:  [lost]ondus ignoti manuf?[lost]
image-002 L6:  [lost] sana cupiens? vocan[lost]
image-002 L7:  [lost]erunt? hic mundi p(er)?[lost]
image-002 L8:  [lost]em nudis alimenta [lost]
image-002 L9:  [lost]ummos miser[abraded] carce[lost]   (bottom of tile)

FACE 1 — image-003 (lower tile; lines from top of image-003). image-003 L1-L2 repeat image-002 L8-L9 (overlap).

image-003 L1:  = image-002 L8
image-003 L2:  = image-002 L9: [lost]ummos miser[two or three letters abraded: "ter"/"is"?] carce[lost]
image-003 L3:  {I}g[abraded: "ne"/"ni"?] torquentur? stab[lost]
image-003 L4:  [lost]cenius? sup(er)at mina[lost]
image-003 L5:  [lost]is in amore vite sem[lost]
image-003 L6:  [lost]stquam latus omne v[lost]
image-003 L7:  [lost]quitur iocando? corpor[lost]

Notes face 1:
- image-002 L4: the red T is two lines high and stands above the line; "ortor" follows in black, then "ir" or "it" at the cut.
- image-002 L5: last visible word begins "manu" + tall letter (f or s with ligature); "manus" or "manuf…".
- image-002 L6: "cupiens" is abraded in its second half ("cupie" clear, then two damaged letters); the word before, "sana", may be the end of a longer word whose beginning is lost at the left.
- image-002 L7: first word ends "-erunt" or "-erint"/"-etunt"; last sign is p with a cross-stroke through the descender (p(er)/p(ro)) followed by one or two minims at the cut.
- image-003 L3: the red I stands in the left margin, two lines high; after "g" the surface is torn. "torquentur" has an abbreviation mark at the end and the middle letters are abraded: "torq…ntur".
- image-003 L4: first word "[.]cenius"/"[.]centius"; then s-u-p with crossed descender, "-at".
- image-003 L5: "is" then what I read as "in amore" could also be "m amore"/"inamore" (minims run together).
- image-003 L7: "iocando" is damaged; the letters "i/l-o-c-a-n-d-o" are probable, with a possible final abbreviation.

FACE 2 — image-005 (upper tile; lines from top of image-005)

image-005 L1:  [upper halves cut away; lower halves suggest] …er? eum et ..ico? monu?[lost]
image-005 L2:  [lost]egnat simul et creat[lost]
image-005 L3:  [lost]men. [RUBRIC in red:] In p(ri)mo No?[lost]
image-005 L4:  [lost]aurentius dignus sac[lost]
image-005 L5:  [lost]nas qui vicit ignium [lost]
image-005 L6:  [lost]onu(m). {H}ic unus est e[lost]
image-005 L7:  [lost]olumnis lucidis qu[lost]
image-005 L8:  [lost]imulq(ue) fecit opifex. {I or L, red, only left part visible}[lost]
image-005 L9:  [lost]ens felicis dogma ma[lost]
image-005 L10: [cropped at tile edge; = image-006 L3]

FACE 2 — image-006 (lower tile; lines from top of image-006). image-006 L1-L2 repeat image-005 L8-L9 (overlap).

image-006 L1:  = image-005 L8
image-006 L2:  = image-005 L9
image-006 L3:  [lost]ebet in tanta? sanctitate? [lost]
image-006 L4:  [lost]do furis hostis impie [one letter at edge: "f"/"s"?][lost]
image-006 L5:  [lost]incere qui dans? mercede(m)?[lost]
image-006 L6:  [lost]onat martyre(m). {P}recla[lost]
image-006 L7:  [lost]o regi n(ost)ro p(er)petuo qu[lost]

Notes face 2:
- image-005 L3: the rubric reads "In p" with superscript i and abbreviation stroke, "mo", then a red capital that is "N" or "H" with a small "o", cut at the edge.
- image-005 L4: a pale pink "T" lies between L3 and L4 under/behind the black text; I take it as offset from another leaf.
- image-005 L6: "[.]onu(m)" has a stroke over the final letters; could be "-oru(m)" or "-onu(m)"; a small loss sits above "ic unus".
- image-005 L8: the red letter at the right edge is cut by the joint; it is two lines high and begins the next sentence, which continues in L9 with "[.]ens".
- image-006 L3: a narrow loss runs through the middle of the line; "in tanta" is read from minims (could be "intima", "in tanta", "in tuta"); "sanctitate" could be "sacitate"/"s(an)c(t)itate" — an abbreviated form, with a further letter at the edge.
- image-006 L4: "furis" might be "fures"/"furens" with abbreviation; I see f-u-r-i/e-s.
- image-006 L5: "[.]incere" has an abbreviation stroke over the last letters ("-cere"/"-cer(e)t"?); "dans" could be "datis"/"dat is".
- image-006 L6: "martyre" has a stroke above the end: "martyre(m)".

4. LIMITATIONS
- Every line is incomplete on both sides and the top line of each face is cut through; no complete clause survives across a line break, so the readings cannot be joined into continuous text without loss.
- Face 1 lines 5-11 are abraded; several readings there rest on letter outlines.
- The relation between the two faces (same leaf, order) is not established by the images.
- This is an unverified image reading.

Reader activity: opened PROMPT.md; image-001.jpg through image-006.jpg (all six). packet.json not opened.
